paper.title: Phased Exploration with Greedy Exploitation in Stochastic Combinatorial Partial Monitoring Games

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic combinatorial partial monitoring (CPM) game with linear feedback
unmapped: Adversary outcomes theta(t) i.i.d. from unknown distribution on [0,1]^n; feedback is M_x theta(t) for known matrices M_x
Expected reward rbar(x, theta*) depends only on mean theta* (Assumption 1) and is R-Lipschitz in theta (Assumption 3)
Learner action set X arbitrary (possibly exponentially large, infinite or continuous); reward function and M_x known; argmax oracle used
Existence of a global observable set sigma with M_sigma full column rank (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: The adversary fixes a distribution $p$ on $[0,1]^n$ before start of the game ... The learner chooses $x(t) \in \mathcal{X}$ and gets reward $r(x(t),\theta(t))$ ... the learner receives, as feedback, a linear transformation of $\theta(t)$ ... $M_{x(t)} \cdot \theta(t)$. ... $R(T)= T \cdot \bar{r}(x^*,\theta^*_p) - \sum_{t=1}^T \E [\bar{r}(x(t), \theta^*_p)]$

unmapped: Adversary outcomes i.i.d. on [0,1]^n with linear feedback M_x theta
Expected reward depends only on mean and is R-Lipschitz; learner knows R, beta_sigma, R_max, |sigma|
Existence of a global observable set (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: Consider Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} run with knowledge of the number $T$ of rounds.

algorithms.name: PEGE (Phased Exploration with Greedy Exploitation) framework

bound.expression_latex: R_{max} |\sigma| T^{2/3} + 2 R \beta_{\sigma} T^{2/3} \sqrt{ \log 2e^2  + 2 \log T}  + R_{max}

symbols.R_max: maximum expected reward over actions and outcomes
symbols.n_sigma: size |sigma| of the global observable set
symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on transformation matrices of the global observable set (Eq. global-bound)

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (mean-dependent expected reward, global observable set, R-Lipschitz expected reward with R = L_lip)

source.label: thm:distributionindependentregret
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= \log a$, $\alpha=1/2$ and $\beta=0$, and the online game is played over $T$ rounds, we get the following bound on expected regret: $R(T) \le R_{max} |\sigma| T^{2/3} + 2 R \beta_{\sigma} T^{2/3} \sqrt{ \log 2e^2  + 2 \log T}  + R_{max}$

results.notes: Algorithm parameters do not depend on T, so marked anytime (delta = 1/(KT) is only in the analysis). Paper's R is the Lipschitz constant, mapped to L_lip. Regret defined through expected rewards -> pseudo_regret. Proof is approximate (K ~ T^{1/(1+alpha)}).

symbols.sum_sigma_Delta: sum of gaps Delta_x over actions x in the global observable set sigma
symbols.beta_sigma: constant depending on transformation matrices of the global observable set

conditions: Assumptions 1-3; unique optimal action not required

source.label: thm:distributiondependentregret1
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= h \cdot a$, for a tuning parameter $h>0$, $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=1$, ... $R(T) \le \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \left(\dfrac{\log T}{h} \right)^2 + \dfrac{4 \sqrt{2 \pi} e^2 R \Delta_{max} \beta_{\sigma}}{\Delta} e^{\frac{h^2 (2 R^2 \beta^2_{\sigma})}{\Delta^2}}$.

results.notes: Paper's Delta is the smallest positive gap (Delta_min); R mapped to L_lip.

symbols.sum_sigma_Delta: sum of gaps Delta_x over actions in sigma

tuning: C(a) = h*a with 0 < h < Delta^2/(4 R^2 beta_sigma^2)

source.label: thm:distributiondependentregret2
source.quote: When Algorithm~\ref{alg:PhaseForced} is initialized with the parameters $C(a)= h \cdot a$, for a tuning parameter $0<h< \frac{\Delta^2}{4 R^2 \beta^2_{\sigma}}$, $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$, ... $R(T) \le \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \dfrac{\log T}{h} + \dfrac{2 e^2 \Delta_{max}}{\frac{\Delta^2}{4 R^2 \beta^2_{\sigma}} - h}$

results.notes: Appendix theorem; tuning requires knowledge of a gap-dependent bound on h.

bound.expression_latex: B_1(T) = 2(2 R \beta_\sigma |\sigma|^2 R^2_{max} T)^{2/3} \sqrt{\log (4e^2 T^3}) + R_{max}

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: If Assumption 4 fails, then the expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} is bounded as $R(T) \le B_1(T)$.

bound.expression_latex: B_2(T) = \frac{256 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2}{\Delta^2} \log \frac{512 e^2 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2 T}{\Delta^2} R_{max} |\sigma| + \sum_{x \in \sigma} \Delta_x \frac{36 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2 \log T}{\Delta^2} + \frac{8 e^2 R^2 \beta_\sigma^2}{\Delta^2} + R_{max}

symbols.sum_sigma_Delta: sum of gaps over actions in sigma

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: If Assumption 4 holds, then the expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:combined} is bounded as R(T) \le B_2(T) if T_1(\delta) < T_0

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: R(T) \le ... O(T^{2/3} \log T) & \text{ if } \ T_0 \le T_1(\delta)
